text: This is LeaseLeak. Drop in a rent roll — this one is sixteen units across three buildings — and five seconds later you know it is leaking twenty-nine thousand dollars a year.
caption: Drop a rent roll in. Five seconds later: $29,280 a year, left on the table.

text: Every unit is checked against HUD's published Fair Market Rent for its exact ZIP code and bedroom count. Twelve of sixteen are under it. Everything on this page is computed in your browser from public data. Nothing is estimated.
caption: Every unit vs. HUD's Fair Market Rent for its ZIP and bedroom count. All computed in the browser from public data.

text: Then comes the part code cannot do. Gemini reads every figure the engine produced and writes the plan: three things to do this month, in order, with the numbers that justify each one.
caption: Then the AI: Gemini reads every figure and writes the plan — three things to do this month, with the numbers behind each.

text: The model is not allowed to compute anything. Every figure it writes is checked back against the engine, and anything that does not match is flagged. Tenant names never leave the browser.
caption: The model computes nothing. Every figure it writes is checked back against the engine; mismatches are flagged. Tenant names never leave the browser.

text: You can ask it anything. Which increases should I skip? Unit six, where the proposed rent is fifty-four percent of the local median income. And unit A three, where one move-out takes a hundred and seven months to recoup. Five of five figures verified.
caption: “Which increases would you skip?” Unit 6: a 54% rent burden. Unit A3: 107 months to recoup a move-out. 5 of 5 figures verified.

text: Underneath the plan is the whole audit. Building grades. Unit by unit against the benchmark. Twelve months of cash flow. The seasonal calendar, turnover risk, and the voucher option.
caption: Under the plan: building grades, unit by unit, twelve months of cash flow, the seasonal calendar, turnover risk, vouchers.

text: And the renewal letters, written. Capped, never above the benchmark, a term that ends in the seasonal peak. Ten letters, one PDF.
caption: The renewal letters — capped, never above the benchmark, timed to the seasonal peak. Ten letters, one PDF.

text: Real exports are messy. This one has no ZIP column and headers our parser has never seen. The AI maps the columns, the Census geocoder finds the ZIPs, and the same twenty-nine thousand dollars comes back.
caption: A messy export: no ZIP column, unknown headers. AI maps the columns, the Census geocoder finds the ZIPs — same $29,280.

text: LeaseLeak. Code decides every number. AI decides what matters. Free for up to five units, at leaseleak dot vercel dot app.
